prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to eliminate chosen proteins

statement.case_for: After the full first round my preferred configuration is unchanged: B027 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The mechanism is the kind I can state in physical terms: a small molecule holds a target and an E3 ligase at a productive distance, ubiquitin transfer follows from that proximity, and the proteasome does the rest. It was demonstrated in vitro, in cells and structurally, and it has been reproduced by many independent groups. Four of eight members, including the chair, now name the same trio, and those who do not choose it as a preferred configuration still list it as an alternative (Aili, Sparr, Somfai, Zou), so no member rejects it on scientific grounds. Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated the PROTAC concept; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which turned a notorious drug into a mechanism we can write down and which underlies the glue branch. One citation phrased around recruitment of E3 ligases by small molecules covers both branches without naming a fourth person.
statement.case_against: The reservations that remain are real. No degrader is approved, and the clinical record I would use to judge maturity is described from memory by every member, including me, so I cannot confirm it. Credit is crowded: Ciulli, Sakamoto, Ito, Kim and Gray have genuine claims, and a three-name cut will look arbitrary to some. A single citation can be read as merging two discoveries made by different groups at different times. I accept that a committee could reasonably defer; I judge that the mechanistic and priority case is firmer than for the other shortlisted ballots, but I have not seen the expert reports in this round and I hold the position with that limit.

responses.point: Andrei supports B027 only as a second part with Crews and Handa, omitting Deshaies, and pairs it with Liu alone for base editing (B038).
responses.response: I agree with Andrei on the science of both parts but not on the structure. Dropping Deshaies removes one of the two people who conceived and first demonstrated heterobifunctional degraders; the 2001 concept paper came from Crews and Deshaies together, and I cannot write a PROTAC citation that omits one of them without a priority argument I do not have. A trio that includes Handa already fits the three-person limit, so there is no capacity reason to cut him. A two-part prize pairing degraders with base editing also joins two different fields, and Andrei himself says the pairing may reflect the cap more than scientific logic. I would rather keep one coherent achievement. If B027 is not carried, I would find B038 with Liu alone the next most defensible configuration, which is why I now list it as an alternative; my earlier worry about the 2020 CRISPR prize is a timing argument, not a reason to reject the deaminase chemistry.

responses.point: Heiner moved his third name from Ciulli to Handa but concedes that merging the PROTAC and cereblon-glue stories in one citation risks combining two discoveries.
responses.response: This is the question I would put to the committee. My answer is that the two branches share one principle, induced proximity between a target and an E3 ligase, and the citation should be written at that level so that it does not claim they were one discovery. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made degraders drug-like and are important, but they refine a concept that Crews and Deshaies had already shown, whereas Handa's cereblon work explained a clinical drug that had no mechanism. If the committee decides to restrict the prize to PROTACs, Ciulli replaces Handa and I would support that, but then the reports must say why the glue branch is left out.

responses.point: Emma prefers B062 with Cullis, Madden and Hope, favouring the early Vancouver encapsulation and ionizable-lipid principle over the later library and siRNA work.
responses.response: Emma has answered the chair's question about what the citation honours, and her self-assembly argument is more persuasive to me than the formulation objection raised by Johan, Peter and Xiaodong; the pKa-switch design principle is physical chemistry. My difficulty remains priority and fit. She concedes that her trio leaves out Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan, and Daniel's trio differs from hers only a round ago, so credit is unsettled in a way it is not for B027, where four members converged on the same three names. I keep B062 as an alternative, not as my preference.

responses.point: Daniel concedes that his trio omits later optimisation and siRNA translation and argues that maturity risk is nil for lipid nanoparticles because clinical use is proven.
responses.response: I accept that maturity favours B062 over B027, and that is the strongest point against my own preference. But maturity of impact is not the only criterion; credit assignment decides whether the citation can be written defensibly, and Daniel's own concession that his trio leaves out people with real claims shows that is not resolved. The overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize concerns the cargo and not the carrier, as he and Emma say, so I do not treat it as a blocker. On balance I weigh a clearer mechanism and attribution above clinical proof, and I would not oppose B062 if the committee could settle three names.

responses.point: Johan names the same B027 trio and holds Car-Parrinello (B049) as his own field-based first choice, noting that it has almost no support.
responses.response: Johan's candour about field loyalty is useful, and I share the discipline of testing my own preference the same way. For my part I note that my earlier first choice, Gray and Winkler (B026), found no support and I have dropped it. We agree that the B027 trio is the most plausible place for convergence, and I take his point that the clinical risk is the main reason a prize could be early.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports treat PROTACs and cereblon-based glues as one achievement or two, which decides whether Handa and the E3-recruitment wording belong in one citation.
Whether the lack of an approved degrader should delay recognition; clinical status is recalled from memory by all members and is unverified.
Whether Ciulli or Sakamoto has a stronger claim than a named laureate; I cannot resolve this without the reports.
Whether the committee would accept B062 if three names could be agreed, since it is the more mature candidacy.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict or recusal need arises for any shortlisted candidate. I remain Secretary and a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, which bears on no candidate. My own research on respiratory-chain proton transfer is not close to B027, B038 or B062.
